quote: In the case of the human person: first its body is created from the dust, and afterward the power of life is given to it, and this is the being of the soul. Accordingly Moses said about the beasts, "Its blood is its life." But in the case of the human person its being is incorporeal and immortal and has a great superiority over the body, to the same extent as incorporeal form surpasses the corporeal.

The troubling utterance is the following: "The soul of all flesh is the blood" — behold an extremely difficult passage, which has shaken those who did not understand it! … According to my measure of understanding, and with prayer for help in the knowledge of the Divine utterances … I have observed that incorporeal things are given the same names as corporeal things, and thus corporeal things are related to the outer man, while those bearing the same names as the corporeal are related to the inner man. Scripture says that in man there are two. … Therefore in each of us there are two men. Why does the Holy Scripture say that the soul of all flesh is the blood? This is a difficult question. Just as the outer man is homonymous with the inner one, so also with respect to the parts of the body. One may say that each part of the body of the outer man is homonymous with the corresponding part…
